Identity.History: The Scythians were Iranian-speaking nomadic peoples who dominated much of the Eurasian steppe from roughly the 8th to 3rd centuries BC. Famous for mounted archery, mobility, and elaborate goldwork, they controlled trade routes stretching between the Black Sea and Central Asia. Scythian groups fought Persians, Greeks, and neighboring steppe peoples, while also trading extensively with settled civilizations before their power declined and fragmented.
